messages:
Maya: Heads-up: we need to rotate the infra deploy credentials tonight. Release at 20:30 UTC — want to avoid an automatic canary rollback during the cutover.
Sam: What's the plan? full swap or shadow rotate?
Maya: Shadow rotate. Create new key in SecretsManager, stage it as AWSCURRENT after validation, then point deploy-bot to the new version. Minimal downtime.
Nina: Can we do the SecretsManager swap without touching the deploy job mid-canary?
Julian: Yes — deploy-bot reads secret by version stage. We'll add a job env: DEPLOY_SECRET_VERSION_STAGE=AWSCURRENT. When we flip stage, the job picks up the current secret for new runs; existing in-progress canaries keep their in-memory creds.
Sam: So timeline: 20:30 release -> canary runs -> if green, at 21:15 we promote new secret -> 21:20 run quick auth check on a staged canary?
Maya: More like: promote at 21:00 maintenance slot, then run a single-auth smoke canary (5m). If smoke passes, flip global and update release notes. If fails, demote stage and rollback promotion.
Julian: We should also add a targeted deploy-bot rule: if canary failure reason is Auth/STS 403/401, do not trigger full rollback for 10 minutes while ops investigates. We won't touch other failure modes.
Nina: Agreed but annotate the release run: add label `iam-rotation_hold=true` so oncall knows we've suspended auth-triggered rollback.
deploy-bot: change created: "smoke-rotate-1765559999" by Maya. Default canary: 10m. Canary rollback_on_any_failure=true
Sam: Terraform plan pointer (for audit):
```
resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "infra_deploy_v2" {
  secret_id     = aws_secretsmanager_secret.infra_deploy.id
  secret_string = jsonencode({ key = "<new-access-key>" })
}
```
Maya: I'll run the apply in the maintenance slot if release goes green. If release fails, we will not touch secrets.
Julian: Ops checklist I'm creating:
- create secret version (Maya)
- hold policy: add `iam-rotation_hold` to release metadata (Nina)
- deploy-bot exception: ignore auth failures for 10m (Julian)
- promote secret stage to AWSCURRENT (Maya)
- run 5m smoke canary, check auth logs (Sam)
- update release notes + flip DEPLOY_SECRET_VERSION_STAGE if needed (Maya)
- remove deploy-bot exception (Julian)
Nina: Who owns the deploy-bot exception?
Julian: I'll own it. I'll make it 15m TTL to be safe.
Sam: What are rollback criteria? If more than 3 auth failures in smoke canary or >25% auth error rate across canaries, revert stage and trigger rollback.
Maya: Yep. Also escalate to paging if we see 5+ distinct hosts failing auth after promotion.
Nina: Add a short blurb to the release notes and PR: "Secret rotation scheduled post-cutover; temporary auth-failure hold applied for investigation."
Maya: Adding now.
Sam: Will we pin the deploy job to old secret for active canaries? Or rely on in-flight creds staying valid?
Julian: We rely on in-flight creds. Pinning would require duplicating jobs. Simpler to let running tasks complete and new runs pick up AWSCURRENT.
Maya: OK. Final owners: Maya=secret apply & notes, Julian=deploy-bot exception, Sam=smoke canary checks, Nina=release metadata.
deploy-bot: note: while exception active, alerts still post to #eng-oncall with tag [iam-rotation_hold].
Nina: I'll update the PR description and mention @support-team for customer visibility.
Maya: ETA: create secret version 21:00 UTC, promote 21:05 UTC if release healthy; smoke canary 21:05-21:10. If all green, full flip 21:15 and remove exception at 21:30.
Sam: Sounds good. I'll monitor logs and post a short shard-level auth summary after smoke.
Maya: I'll post a 30m readiness message before creating the secret.
Julian: Opening the deploy-bot change now and tagging @eng-oncall. :white_check_mark:
Sam: LGTM.
